newsitem.title: QATAR: Airlines hike fares from Qatar to India.
newsitem.headline: Airlines hike fares from Qatar to India.

text.p: Airlines flying to India from or via Qatar have raised their fares by up to 56 percent and levied a fuel surcharge to make up for an increase in fuel costs, travel industry executives said on Tuesday.

Qatar Airways, the oil and gas-rich state's two-year-old flag carrier, had previously resisted the price rise, but agreed to the move after a unanimous decision by the Yield Improvement Committee, made up of airlines operating to India.
"A round-trip economy class excursion fare to Bombay has gone up to 2,340 riyals ($643) in keeping with the...decision taken by other airlines," a Qatar Airways official said.
The airline previously charged 1,500 riyals for the ticket.
"This amounts to a 56 percent rise in Qatar Airways fares and a 20 percent (rise) in the case of other airlines operating from Doha," a travel agency executive said.

Qatar Airways former chief executive, Sheikh Ali bin Jabr al-Thani, who was dismissed last month, had resisted attempts to raise fares to create what he called a "niche" for the carrier in the Gulf's burgeoning airline market.
"Now, after the exit of its former chief executive, Qatar Airways has joined up with other Gulf and Indian subcontinent's airlines to follow a uniform fare level," the travel agency executive said.
Airlines operating between Doha and India include Gulf Air, Qatar Airways, Air India, Emirates, Kuwait Airways, Saudi Arabian Airlines, Pakistan International Airlines and Air Lanka.
Industry sources said fares to other destinations, such as Pakistan, Phillipines, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Egypt, were also under review and were expected to rise.
The International Air Transport Association on November 15 proposed a global three percent passenger fare increase to make up for a rise of more than 40 percent in fuel costs this year.
